summary: Small Claude-generated interlingual harmonization snapshot. It includes PROGRAM, CORPUS_MAP, ISLAND_ATLAS, STATUS, an Interslavic term-decision extraction JSON/script, a CPU-only union-term-spine builder, and the UNION_TERM_SPINE_20260704 MD/JSON artifact. It synthesizes the project as a set of language-family/register construction islands around source shelves, term spines, proof grammar, script sidecars, review packets, and pilot gates.
important_findings: Source availability is treated as the real gating axis for bridge/register construction.
Standard/script unity is treated as the main build-type discriminator: zonal bridge, controlled register, script bridge, or local standard.
The union term spine v1 reports 138 unique concepts across four explicit lane spines, with only 17 concepts present in all four lanes and 32 present in at least three lanes.
Dominance drift is identified as a recurring risk across human bridge construction and machine representation spaces.
The snapshot explicitly records zero external validation/approval as an important limitation.
public_caveat: Provisional methodology and synthesis artifact only. Not native-speaker approval, not term approval, not source certification, not language synchronization proof, not a critical edition, and not a completed framework paper.
recommended_public_description: This compact support packet preserves a 2026-07-04 interlingual harmonization synthesis generated from the project’s language-methodology logs. It contains a corpus map, programme proposal, island atlas, and a first union term spine across language-family/register lanes. It is useful as methodology evidence for the interlanguage record and for future framework-paper work, but it does not approve terminology, certify translations, or validate intelligibility claims.
